outcome: No result settling the stated 3^d conjecture (or any new case of it) has appeared since 26 January 2024; the general conjecture remains open, and the sole in-window paper found proves a different (though related) flag-vector conjecture for a restricted polytope class, not the 3^d conjecture itself.
summary: Kalai's 3^d conjecture (every centrally symmetric d-dimensional polytope has at least 3^d nonempty faces, with equality only for Hanner polytopes) remains open in general. The triage record flagged a July 2025 preprint by Arnon Chor (arXiv:2507.22284, 'Kalai's flag conjecture for locally anti-blocking polytopes'), asking whether it constitutes progress on the 3^d conjecture as stated. Having read the paper's introduction, this is a related-but-different problem, not a case of the stated conjecture: it proves 'Kalai's flag conjecture' (Conjecture 1.3 in the paper), a separate, later conjecture also attributed to Kalai, which counts flags (maximal chains of faces, one per dimension) rather than the total number of nonempty faces that the 3^d conjecture counts. The paper's own introduction states that the 3^d conjecture itself for locally anti-blocking polytopes was 'recently' proved by Sanyal and Winter, and independently by Chambers and Portnoy (arXiv:2211.09215) -- and both of those results predate the frozen revision. Chambers-Portnoy's note first appeared on arXiv in November 2022, and Sanyal-Winter's paper (arXiv:2308.02909) was first submitted 5 August 2023, with its final v3 revision posted 21 April 2024 -- the revision postdates the snapshot, but the first public written argument (v1, per section 6.3's dating rule) does not, so this case-settling result is 'open_stale' relative to the frozen date, not new. No further case of the actual 3^d conjecture, no counterexample, and no full resolution has appeared in the window. Gil Kalai's own blog (gilkalai.wordpress.com), including a February 2026 'Updates and Plans' post, was checked for any mention of new developments on this specific conjecture; none was found. No AI system is credited anywhere: the Chor paper's acknowledgements name only human collaborators and funding bodies, and no search turned up any AI-related claim connected to this conjecture.
competing_reading: One could argue the flag conjecture, because it dominates the ordinary face count in certain ways for the same restricted class of polytopes (locally anti-blocking) and reaffirms Hanner polytopes as the unique extremizers, is close enough in spirit to count as 'progress' on the broader research program Kalai's 3^d conjecture belongs to. But per the scope rule in section 3.1, the test is whether the result changes what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry specifically -- and it does not, since it is a strictly different quantity (flags vs. total faces) with its own separate conjecture status, and the 3^d-conjecture case for this same polytope class was already resolved (and already stale) before the window began.
what_would_settle_it: A published or arXiv-posted proof (or disproof) of the 3^d conjecture in full generality, or a proof/disproof for a new class of centrally symmetric polytopes not already covered by the pre-2024 Sanyal-Winter/Chambers-Portnoy results, dated after 26 January 2024, would change this record's status to partial, claimed, or resolved as appropriate.
